chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

If you want to shroud him, then if you are able that there be in his shroud a clean garment in which he used to perform salat (prayer), then do so, for it is recommended that he be shrouded in what he used to perform salat (prayer) in.
And [regarding] that in which he used to perform sawm (fasting), should he be shrouded in it? He said: “I like that shroud,” meaning a shirt.
I said: Should he be wrapped in three garments? He said: “There is no harm in it, and the shirt is more beloved to me.”

key_terms.تُكَفِّنَهُ: to shroud the deceased in a kafan
key_terms.قَمِيصًا: a shirt used as part of the shroud

ai.seo_question: Is it recommended to shroud the deceased in clothes he used to pray in?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses recommended rulings concerning the kafan of the deceased. It states that it is preferable to shroud the deceased in a clean garment in which he used to perform salat (prayer), and it indicates preference for including a shirt among the burial garments.
